findings.title: Worst-case impact exceeds human pain thresholds
findings.detail: Worst case: arm into the chest at 4.79 m/s transfers 86.9 J against a 1.57 J limit (55x).
evidence: Over the limit: Abdomen, Chest, Hand and fingers, Lower arm and wrist, Thigh and knee, Upper arm and elbow
Safe speed for this body region: 0.64 m/s
findings.fix: Cap speed in shared zones at the safe speed Caziel reports, keep a collision monitor on every velocity path, and enforce the cap below ROS (drives or safety PLC).

changes.what: Retargeted from /cmd_vel to /cmd_vel_smoothed and set requires_approval
changes.why: Commands on this mapping now pass through the collision monitor, so a nudge still works but cannot drive into a person.
The arm can reach a person standing next to the robot, and MoveIt does not see people. A human confirms each pick near staff.
Raw joint trajectories skip MoveIt. Replay taught motions through MoveIt (ExecuteTrajectory or MoveGroup) so collision checks and velocity scaling apply.
Wildcard parameter writes let a cloud message raise speed limits or disable collision zones. Use Nav2 speed filter zones for 'slow down in busy aisles' instead.

changes.what: Limited lifecycle control to 5 non-safety nodes
changes.why: Operators can still restart a hung Nav2 node, but cannot shut down the collision monitor.

changes.what: Enabled SROS2 (Enforce) with a dedicated bridge enclave
changes.why: Without DDS security, anything on the warehouse network can publish to /cmd_vel directly.
The maintenance tablet reaches it through the authenticated bridge instead of the open LAN.
Same cap on the planner side, so the smoother is not the only thing holding it.
0.25 m/s keeps a 116 kg base inside the transient-contact limit for the thigh and knee (safe speed 0.29 m/s).
It published to fleet/{thing}/cmd/param, which the bridge no longer accepts.

changes.what: Denied iot:Publish everywhere except 3 tool topic(s)
changes.why: The tool role could publish anywhere under fleet/*. Rewriting one tool's code would have handed that over. Now the role can only send what the tools are written to send.

changes.what: Added explicit-deny guardrail (raw topics, code deploy, agent tool code)
changes.why: fleet-tools-role was flagged for CZL-001, CZL-002, CZL-003, CZL-004.

manual: KX-1 mobile manipulator: the base controller still allows 2.0 m/s. ROS parameters can be changed by anything that runs on the robot. Enforce the shared-zone speed limit in the motor drives or a safety PLC as well.
KX-1 mobile manipulator: generate keys with `ros2 security create_keystore` and `create_enclave`, then re-run `caziel snapshot` to confirm SROS2 is on.
release-pipeline-role: limit the OIDC trust policy to refs/heads/main and require signed Greengrass components. Caziel marked its code-deploy finding as accepted on that condition; check it is true.
